text:
Florida arrives at Chicago on two straight losses, 5-1 at Ottawa and 4-0 at Pittsburgh, where Arturs Silovs stopped all 26 shots. The Panthers are 3-2-0 in their last five and are missing Brad Marchand and Aleksander Barkov. Carter Verhaeghe has stepped in beside Sam Reinhart and Brady Tkachuk, and Lars Eller is up to 17:21 a night from 12:14. Chicago has lost two in a row and three of five, most recently 4-1 to Montreal, and is without Bowen Byram, whose minutes are going to Wyatt Kaiser.

Our numbers say the Blackhawks are better than their record. Their goal difference is -18 on -8.4 expected, and finishing and goaltending have both cost them. Even so, Florida has taken 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, Chicago 41%. We have it 3.28 to 2.85 for the Panthers. Florida takes 5.7 penalties a game, which hands out power plays, though Chicago's power play is generating only 0.45 expected goals a game. In net, projected starters Akira Schmid (-3.1 goals saved above expected this season) and Spencer Knight (-1.1, but +11.1 last season) have both struggled.

Bedard is our top Chicago pick at 34% to score and 70% for a point, and The Athletic's Scott Powers posted that Tyler Bertuzzi replaces Patrick Kane on his line. Verhaeghe plays his 500th NHL game. Among our under-the-radar picks, Brady Tkachuk has 4.8 expected goals over his last 10 (32% to score), and Roman Kantserov is 53% for a point.
